alternateQuestions.calculationDraft: Correct: To find the temperature of the hot reservoir, we use the formula: efficiency = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot). Given efficiency = 0.4 and T_cold = 300K, 0.4 = 1 - (300 / T_hot), so T_hot = 300 / (1 - 0.4) = 300 / 0.6 = 500K. Distractor A: Student calculates T_hot as 300 / 0.4 = 750K. Distractor B: Student thinks efficiency is directly proportional to the temperatures, so T_hot = efficiency * T_cold = 0.4 * 300 = 120K. Distractor C: Student calculates T_hot as 300 / (1 - 0.4) but uses the wrong efficiency value, 0.5, so T_hot = 300 / (1 - 0.5) = 300 / 0.5 = 600K.

relatedContent.conceptSummary: The Carnot Cycle is a theoretical thermodynamic cycle that is the most efficient possible cycle for converting thermal energy into mechanical work. The efficiency of the Carnot Cycle is given by the formula: efficiency = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot), where T_cold is the temperature of the cold reservoir and T_hot is the temperature of the hot reservoir.
